    93→// parseResourceAttributes parses OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env var into attribute.KeyValue slice.
    94→// Format: "key1=value1,key2=value2"
    95→func parseResourceAttributes() []attribute.KeyValue {
    96→	envVal := os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES")
    97→	if envVal == "" {
    98→		return nil
    99→	}
   100→
   101→	var attrs []attribute.KeyValue
   102→	pairs := strings.Split(envVal, ",")
   103→	for _, pair := range pairs {
   104→		pair = strings.TrimSpace(pair)
   105→		if pair == "" {
   106→			continue
   107→		}
   108→		kv := strings.SplitN(pair, "=", 2)
   109→		if len(kv) == 2 {
   110→			key := strings.TrimSpace(kv[0])
   111→			value := strings.TrimSpace(kv[1])
   112→			if key != "" {
   113→				attrs = append(attrs, attribute.String(key, value))
   114→			}
   115→		}
   116→	}
   117→	return attrs
   118→}
   119→
   120→// parseEndpoint normalises an OTLP endpoint string into a bare host:port suitable
   121→// for otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint and a flag indicating whether TLS should be disabled.
   122→//
   123→// Accepted formats:
   124→//
   125→//	"localhost:4317"                 → host="localhost:4317",          insecure=true
   126→//	"http://localhost:4317"          → host="localhost:4317",          insecure=true
   127→//	"https://collector.example:4317" → host="collector.example:4317",  insecure=false
   128→func parseEndpoint(raw string) (host string, insecure bool) {
   129→	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
   130→	if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
   131→		// Not a URL — treat the whole string as host:port (bare address).
   132→		return raw, true
   133→	}
   134→
   135→	// Parsed successfully as a URL with a scheme.
   136→	host = u.Host
   137→	insecure = u.Scheme != "https"
   138→	return host, insecure
   139→}

   141→// Init configures the OTel tracing and metrics subsystem. Thread-safe and idempotent — only the
   142→// first call takes effect. When Enabled is false the global no-op provider remains
   143→// active, so callers can emit spans/events and record metrics safely with zero overhead.
   144→func Init(ctx context.Context, opts Options) error {
   145→	var initErr error
   146→	initOnce.Do(func() {
   147→		if !opts.Enabled {
   148→			telemetryLogger().Info("Telemetry disabled, using no-op provider")
   149→			return
   150→		}
   151→
   152→		// Route OTel SDK errors (export failures, connection issues) through slog
   153→		// so they appear in debug logs alongside our own telemetry messages.
   154→		otel.SetErrorHandler(otel.ErrorHandlerFunc(func(err error) {
   155→			telemetryLogger().Warn("OTel SDK error", "error", err)
   156→		}))
   157→
   158→		serviceName := opts.ServiceName
   159→		if serviceName == "" {
   160→			serviceName = "specstory-cli"
   161→		}
   162→
   163→		// Parse the endpoint to extract a bare host:port for WithEndpoint and
   164→		// determine TLS mode from the scheme. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is
   165→		// conventionally a full URL (e.g. "http://localhost:4317"), but
   166→		// WithEndpoint expects just "host:port".
   167→		host, insecure := parseEndpoint(opts.Endpoint)
   168→
   169→		// Create shared resource for both traces and metrics.
   170→		// Use resource.New() with detectors to pick up OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env var.
   171→		res, err := resource.New(ctx,
   172→			resource.WithFromEnv(),      // OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
   173→			resource.WithTelemetrySDK(), // telemetry.sdk.* attributes
   174→			resource.WithHost(),         // host.* attributes
   175→			resource.WithAttributes(attribute.String("service.name", serviceName)), // explicit service name (can override env)
   176→		)
   177→		if err != nil {
   178→			initErr = fmt.Errorf("create OTel resource: %w", err)
   179→			return
   180→		}
   181→
   182→		// Log the resource attributes for debugging
   183→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Resource attributes created",
   184→			"attributes", res.Attributes(),
   185→			"OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES", os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES"),
   186→		)
   187→
   188→		// Initialize tracing
   189→		if err := initTracing(ctx, host, insecure, res); err != nil {
   190→			initErr = err
   191→			return
   192→		}
   193→
   194→		// Initialize metrics
   195→		if err := initMetrics(ctx, host, insecure, res); err != nil {
   196→			// Roll back tracing initialization to avoid half-initialized state
   197→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Metrics init failed, rolling back tracing", "error", err)
   198→			if traceProvider != nil {
   199→				if shutdownErr := traceProvider.Shutdown(ctx); shutdownErr != nil {
   200→					telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to shutdown trace provider during rollback", "error", shutdownErr)
   201→				}
   202→				traceProvider = nil
   203→				// Use no-op provider instead of nil per OTel documentation
   204→				otel.SetTracerProvider(noop.NewTracerProvider())
   205→			}
   206→			initErr = err
   207→			return
   208→		}
   209→
   210→		metricsEnabled = true
   211→
   212→		// Parse OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and store as common metric attributes.
   213→		// This ensures resource attributes appear as metric tags in backends like Datadog
   214→		// that may not automatically promote resource-level attributes to metric tags.
   215→		commonMetricAttrs = parseResourceAttributes()
   216→		if len(commonMetricAttrs) > 0 {
   217→			telemetryLogger().Debug("Parsed OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES for metrics",
   218→				"count", len(commonMetricAttrs),
   219→				"attributes", commonMetricAttrs,
   220→			)
   221→		}
   222→
   223→		telemetryLogger().Info("Telemetry initialised",
   224→			"endpoint", host,
   225→			"insecure", insecure,
   226→			"serviceName", serviceName,
   227→		)
   228→	})
   229→
   230→	return initErr
   231→}

   233→// initTracing sets up the trace provider and exporter.
   234→func initTracing(ctx context.Context, host string, insecure bool, res *resource.Resource) error {
   235→	exporterOpts := []otlptracegrpc.Option{
   236→		otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint(host),
   237→	}
   238→	if insecure {
   239→		exporterOpts = append(exporterOpts, otlptracegrpc.WithInsecure())
   240→	}
   241→
   242→	exporter, err := otlptracegrpc.New(ctx, exporterOpts...)
   243→	if err != nil {
   244→		return fmt.Errorf("create OTLP trace exporter: %w", err)
   245→	}
   246→
   247→	traceProvider = sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(
   248→		sdktrace.WithBatcher(exporter),
   249→		sdktrace.WithResource(res),
   250→	)
   251→	otel.SetTracerProvider(traceProvider)
   252→
   253→	return nil
   254→}
   255→
   256→// initMetrics sets up the meter provider, exporter, and metric instruments.
   257→func initMetrics(ctx context.Context, host string, insecure bool, res *resource.Resource) error {
   258→	exporterOpts := []otlpmetricgrpc.Option{
   259→		otlpmetricgrpc.WithEndpoint(host),
   260→	}
   261→	if insecure {
   262→		exporterOpts = append(exporterOpts, otlpmetricgrpc.WithInsecure())
   263→	}
   264→
   265→	exporter, err := otlpmetricgrpc.New(ctx, exporterOpts...)
   266→	if err != nil {
   267→		return fmt.Errorf("create OTLP metric exporter: %w", err)
   268→	}
   269→
   270→	meterProvider = sdkmetric.NewMeterProvider(
   271→		sdkmetric.WithResource(res),
   272→		sdkmetric.WithReader(sdkmetric.NewPeriodicReader(exporter,
   273→			sdkmetric.WithInterval(metricExportInterval),
   274→		)),
   275→	)
   276→	otel.SetMeterProvider(meterProvider)
   277→
   278→	meter = meterProvider.Meter("specstory-cli")
   279→
   280→	// Initialize metric instruments
   281→	if err := initMetricInstruments(); err != nil {
   282→		return fmt.Errorf("create metric instruments: %w", err)
   283→	}
   284→
   285→	return nil
   286→}

   419→// Shutdown flushes pending spans/metrics and shuts down both providers.
   420→// Safe to call even when Init was never called or telemetry is disabled.
   421→// For short-lived CLIs, this performs explicit ForceFlush calls before shutdown
   422→// to ensure all data is exported before the process exits.
   423→func Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error {
   424→	var errs []error
   425→
   426→	if traceProvider != nil {
   427→		telemetryLogger().Info("Flushing and shutting down trace provider")
   428→		// ForceFlush ensures all pending spans are exported before shutdown.
   429→		// This is critical for short-lived CLIs that may exit before the
   430→		// periodic exporter has time to run.
   431→		if err := traceProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   432→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to flush trace provider", "error", err)
   433→		}
   434→		if err := traceProvider.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
   435→			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("shutdown trace provider: %w", err))
   436→		}
   437→	}
   438→
   439→	if meterProvider != nil {
   440→		telemetryLogger().Info("Flushing and shutting down meter provider")
   441→		// ForceFlush ensures all pending metrics are exported before shutdown.
   442→		// The periodic reader has a 10-second interval, so without this,
   443→		// metrics from short CLI runs would never be sent.
   444→		if err := meterProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   445→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to flush meter provider", "error", err)
   446→		}
   447→		if err := meterProvider.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
   448→			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("shutdown meter provider: %w", err))
   449→		}
   450→	}
   451→
   452→	return errors.Join(errs...)
   453→}
   454→
   455→// ForceFlush explicitly flushes all pending spans and metrics.
   456→// Call this at the end of short-lived commands to ensure data is exported
   457→// before the command returns. Safe to call when telemetry is disabled.
   458→func ForceFlush(ctx context.Context) error {
   459→	var errs []error
   460→
   461→	if traceProvider != nil {
   462→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Force flushing trace provider")
   463→		if err := traceProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   464→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to force flush trace provider", "error", err)
   465→			errs = append(errs, err)
   466→		}
   467→	}
   468→
   469→	if meterProvider != nil {
   470→		telemetryLogger().Debug("Force flushing meter provider")
   471→		if err := meterProvider.ForceFlush(ctx); err != nil {
   472→			telemetryLogger().Warn("Failed to force flush meter provider", "error", err)
   473→			errs = append(errs, err)
   474→		}
   475→	}
   476→
   477→	return errors.Join(errs...)
   478→}

   482→func Tracer(name string) trace.Tracer {

   484→}

   488→func Meter() metric.Meter {

   495→// ContextWithSessionTrace returns a context that will cause any spans started
   496→// from it to share the same trace ID (derived deterministically from sessionID).
   497→// This groups all spans for a given session into a single trace, even across
   498→// multiple invocations (e.g., in autosave mode where processSingleSession is
   499→// called repeatedly as the session file grows).
   500→func ContextWithSessionTrace(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) context.Context {
   501→	traceID := traceIDFromSessionID(sessionID)
   502→	spanID := spanIDFromSessionID(sessionID)
   503→
   504→	// Create a SpanContext with both deterministic trace ID and span ID.
   505→	// In OpenTelemetry-Go, a SpanContext is only valid if both TraceID and SpanID
   506→	// are valid. We mark it as Remote so child spans inherit the trace ID.
   507→	sc := trace.NewSpanContext(trace.SpanContextConfig{
   508→		TraceID:    traceID,
   509→		SpanID:     spanID,
   510→		TraceFlags: trace.FlagsSampled, // Ensure it's sampled
   511→		Remote:     true,               // Mark as remote parent
   512→	})
   513→
   514→	// Inject the SpanContext as a remote parent so child spans inherit the trace ID
   515→	return trace.ContextWithRemoteSpanContext(ctx, sc)
   516→}
   517→
   518→// traceIDFromSessionID generates a deterministic 16-byte trace ID from a session ID
   519→// by hashing the session ID with SHA-256 and taking the first 16 bytes.
   520→func traceIDFromSessionID(sessionID string) trace.TraceID {
   521→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID))
   522→	var traceID trace.TraceID
   523→	copy(traceID[:], hash[:16])
   524→	return traceID
   525→}
   526→
   527→// spanIDFromSessionID generates a deterministic 8-byte span ID from a session ID
   528→// by hashing the session ID with SHA-256 and taking bytes 16-24.
   529→// This ensures the span ID is different from the trace ID but still deterministic.
   530→func spanIDFromSessionID(sessionID string) trace.SpanID {
   531→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID))
   532→	var spanID trace.SpanID
   533→	copy(spanID[:], hash[16:24])
   534→	return spanID
   535→}

   537→// --- Metric Recording Functions ---
   538→// These are internal functions called by RecordSessionMetrics in session_helpers.go.
   539→// The metricsEnabled check is done once in RecordSessionMetrics.
   540→
   541→// buildMetricAttrs combines specific metric attributes with common attributes from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES.

   600→type TokenUsage struct {

   622→// providerAttrs returns OTel span attributes for provider-specific token fields,
   623→// including only non-zero values to reduce telemetry noise. The prefix is the
   624→// attribute namespace (e.g. "specstory.session.tokens" or "specstory.exchange.tokens").
   625→func (u TokenUsage) providerAttrs(prefix string) []attribute.KeyValue {
   626→	var attrs []attribute.KeyValue
   627→	// Claude Code specific (also used by Droid CLI)
   628→	if u.CacheCreationInputTokens > 0 {

   644→	}
   645→	if u.ThoughtTokens > 0 {
   646→		attrs = append(attrs, attribute.Int(prefix+".thought", u.ThoughtTokens))

   651→	// Droid CLI specific

   654→	}

   184→// --- Exchange Helpers ---
   185→
   186→// extractToolInfo extracts tool usage information from an exchange.
   187→// Returns: comma-separated unique tool names, comma-separated unique tool types, and total tool count.
   188→func extractToolInfo(exchange schema.Exchange) (toolNames string, toolTypes string, toolCount int) {
   189→	nameSet := make(map[string]bool)
   190→	typeSet := make(map[string]bool)
   191→
   192→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   193→		if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.Name != "" {
   194→			toolCount++
   195→			nameSet[msg.Tool.Name] = true
   196→			if msg.Tool.Type != "" {
   197→				typeSet[msg.Tool.Type] = true
   198→			}
   199→		}
   200→	}
   201→
   202→	// Build unique tool names list (sorted for deterministic output)
   203→	var names []string
   204→	for n := range nameSet {
   205→		names = append(names, n)
   206→	}
   207→	sort.Strings(names)
   208→
   209→	// Build unique tool types list (sorted for deterministic output)
   210→	var types []string
   211→	for t := range typeSet {
   212→		types = append(types, t)
   213→	}
   214→	sort.Strings(types)
   215→
   216→	return strings.Join(names, ","), strings.Join(types, ","), toolCount
   217→}
   218→
   219→// extractUserPromptText finds the first user message in an exchange and returns its text content.
   220→func extractUserPromptText(exchange schema.Exchange) string {
   221→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   222→		if msg.Role == schema.RoleUser {
   223→			// Concatenate all text content parts
   224→			var text string
   225→			for _, part := range msg.Content {
   226→				if part.Type == schema.ContentTypeText {
   227→					if text != "" {
   228→						text += "\n"
   229→					}
   230→					text += part.Text
   231→				}
   232→			}
   233→			return text
   234→		}
   235→	}
   236→	return ""
   237→}
   238→
   239→// extractModel finds the model used in an exchange by looking at agent messages.
   240→// Returns the model from the first agent message that has one set.
   241→func extractModel(exchange schema.Exchange) string {
   242→	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   243→		if msg.Role == schema.RoleAgent && msg.Model != "" {
   244→			return msg.Model
   245→		}
   246→	}
   247→	return ""
   248→}

   252→// countSessionMessages counts total messages across all exchanges.
   253→func countSessionMessages(exchanges []schema.Exchange) int {

   257→	}

   259→}

   261→// countSessionTools counts total tools and unique tool types across all exchanges.

   264→	typeSet := make(map[string]bool)

   266→	for _, exchange := range exchanges {

   268→			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.Name != "" {

   270→				if msg.Tool.Type != "" {
   271→					typeSet[msg.Tool.Type] = true
   272→				}
   273→			}
   274→		}
   275→	}
   276→
   277→	return toolCount, len(typeSet)
   278→}

   280→// countExchangeTokens aggregates token usage for a single exchange.
   281→// Handles Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Droid CLI specific token fields.
   282→func countExchangeTokens(exchange schema.Exchange) TokenUsage {

   295→			// Gemini CLI specific

   297→			usage.ThoughtTokens += msg.Usage.ThoughtTokens
   298→			usage.ToolTokens += msg.Usage.ToolTokens
   299→			// Droid CLI specific

   306→// countSessionTokens aggregates token usage across all exchanges in a session.

   308→func countSessionTokens(exchanges []schema.Exchange) TokenUsage {

Here's the full picture of how OTel works in this codebase:

## Package: `pkg/telemetry/`

Two files:

### `telemetry.go` — Core setup

**Initialization** (`Init`):
- Takes `Options{Enabled, Endpoint, ServiceName}` 
- Uses `sync.Once` so it's idempotent (first call wins)
- When disabled, falls back silently to OTel's built-in **no-op provider** — zero overhead, no nil checks needed anywhere
- Parses the endpoint to handle both bare `host:port` and full URLs (`http://`, `https://`)
- Builds an OTel `resource` from env vars (`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`) plus host info

**Two subsystems initialized:**
1. **Tracing** — OTLP gRPC trace exporter → `sdktrace.TracerProvider` set as global
2. **Metrics** — OTLP gRPC metric exporter → `sdkmetric.MeterProvider` with a 10s periodic reader, set as global

**Metric instruments** (`initMetricInstruments`): Creates counters/histograms for:
- `specstory.sessions.processed`, `.exchanges.processed`, `.messages.processed`, `.tools.used`
- `specstory.session.duration` (histogram)
- Token counters per provider (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Droid)

**Session tracing trick** (`ContextWithSessionTrace`): Generates a **deterministic trace ID from the session UUID** via SHA-256. This means repeated invocations of the same session (e.g., in autosave mode) all share one trace in the backend.

**Shutdown/ForceFlush**: Explicitly flushes before shutdown since CLI processes are short-lived and may exit before the 10s periodic export fires.

---

### `stats_helpers.go` — Stats computation & recording

- `ComputeSessionStats` — walks session data to count exchanges, messages, tools, tokens
- `ProcessExchangeSpans` — creates one child span per exchange with attributes (model, prompt text, tool names, token usage); optionally redacts prompts via `noPrompts` flag
- `RecordSessionMetrics` — records all metric counters (gated on `metricsEnabled`)
- Token counting helpers handle all 4 provider flavors

---

### How it's wired in

- `main.go` / commands call `telemetry.Init(ctx, opts)` at startup and `telemetry.Shutdown(ctx)` at exit
- `pkg/config` reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (or config file) to populate `Options.Endpoint`
- `pkg/session/session.go` calls `ComputeSessionStats`, `ProcessExchangeSpans`, and `RecordSessionMetrics` after processing each session

    77→				"capabilityType", bubble.CapabilityType)
    78→			continue
    79→		}
    80→
    81→		// Calculate timestamp from timing info
    82→		timestamp := calculateTimestamp(bubble.TimingInfo)
    83→
    84→		// If this is a user message without a timestamp, use the timestamp from the next assistant message
    85→		// This matches the extension's behavior (see ts-extension/core/utils/conversation.ts:55-72)
    86→		if bubble.Type == 1 && timestamp == "" {
    87→			// Find next assistant message with timestamp
    88→			for j := i + 1; j < len(composer.Conversation); j++ {
    89→				nextBubble := composer.Conversation[j]
    90→				if nextBubble.Type == 2 { // assistant message
    91→					nextTimestamp := calculateTimestamp(nextBubble.TimingInfo)
    92→					if nextTimestamp != "" {
    93→						timestamp = nextTimestamp
    94→						break
    95→					}
    96→				}
    97→			}
    98→		}
    99→
   100→		// Get model name: bubble-level modelInfo > composer-level modelConfig
   101→		modelName := ""
   102→		if bubble.ModelInfo != nil && bubble.ModelInfo.ModelName != "" {
   103→			modelName = bubble.ModelInfo.ModelName
   104→		} else if composerModelName != "" {
   105→			modelName = composerModelName
   106→		}
   107→
   108→		// Build message with model and mode info
   109→		message := schema.Message{
   110→			Role:      getRoleFromType(bubble.Type),
   111→			Timestamp: timestamp,
   112→			Model:     modelName,
   113→			Content: []schema.ContentPart{
   114→				{
   115→					Type: schema.ContentTypeText,
   116→					Text: messageText,
   117→				},
   118→			},
   119→		}
   120→
   121→		// Add mode to metadata for agent messages
   122→		if bubble.Type == 2 && bubble.UnifiedMode != 0 {
   123→			message.Metadata = map[string]interface{}{
   124→				"mode": unifiedModeToString(bubble.UnifiedMode),
   125→			}
   126→		}
   127→
   128→		// If this is a user message and we have pending messages, create an exchange first
   129→		if bubble.Type == 1 && len(currentMessages) > 0 {
   130→			exchange := schema.Exchange{
   131→				Messages: currentMessages,
   132→			}
   133→			sessionData.Exchanges = append(sessionData.Exchanges, exchange)
   134→			currentMessages = nil
   135→		}
   136→
   137→		currentMessages = append(currentMessages, message)
   138→	}
   139→
   140→	// Create final exchange if there are remaining messages
   141→	if len(currentMessages) > 0 {
   142→		exchange := schema.Exchange{
   143→			Messages: currentMessages,
   144→		}
   145→		sessionData.Exchanges = append(sessionData.Exchanges, exchange)
   146→	}
   147→
   148→	// Marshal to JSON for raw data
   149→	rawDataJSON, err := json.Marshal(composer)
   150→	if err != nil {
   151→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal composer to JSON: %w", err)
   152→	}
   153→
   154→	slog.Debug("Converted composer to AgentChatSession",
   155→		"composerID", sessionID,
   156→		"slug", slug,
   157→		"exchanges", len(sessionData.Exchanges))
   158→
   159→	return &spi.AgentChatSession{
   160→		SessionID:   sessionID,
   161→		CreatedAt:   createdAt,
   162→		Slug:        slug,
   163→		SessionData: sessionData,
   164→		RawData:     string(rawDataJSON),
   165→	}, nil
   166→}

   168→// generateSlug creates a slug from the composer name or first user message
   169→func generateSlug(composer *ComposerData) string {
   170→	// Use composer name if available
   171→	if composer.Name != "" {
   172→		return slugify(composer.Name)
   173→	}
   174→
   175→	// Otherwise, use first user message
   176→	for _, bubble := range composer.Conversation {
   177→		if bubble.Type == 1 && bubble.Text != "" {
   178→			// Take first 4 words
   179→			return slugifyText(bubble.Text, 4)
   180→		}
   181→	}
   182→
   183→	// Fallback to composer ID
   184→	return composer.ComposerID
   185→}
   186→
   187→// slugify converts a string to a slug while preserving casing
   188→// The casing is preserved for use in titles, and will be lowercased for filenames by the caller
   189→func slugify(s string) string {
   190→	// Replace spaces with hyphens, keep original casing
   191→	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, " ", "-")
   192→	return s
   193→}
   194→
   195→// slugifyText converts text to a slug using the first N words
   196→func slugifyText(text string, wordCount int) string {
   197→	words := strings.Fields(text)
   198→	if len(words) > wordCount {
   199→		words = words[:wordCount]
   200→	}
   201→	return slugify(strings.Join(words, " "))
   202→}
   203→
   204→// getRoleFromType converts Cursor's message type to schema role
   205→func getRoleFromType(messageType int) string {
   206→	if messageType == 1 {
   207→		return schema.RoleUser
   208→	}
   209→	return schema.RoleAgent
   210→}
   211→
   212→// buildMessageText constructs the full message text including thinking blocks and tool invocations
   213→func buildMessageText(bubble *ComposerConversation, capabilitiesMap map[int]*CapabilityData, toolRegistry *ToolRegistry, composerVersion int) string {
   214→	var parts []string
   215→
   216→	// Add thinking block if present
   217→	if bubble.Thinking != nil && bubble.Thinking.Text != "" {
   218→		thinkingBlock := fmt.Sprintf("<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>\n%s</details></think>", bubble.Thinking.Text)
   219→		parts = append(parts, thinkingBlock)
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	// Process tool invocations if this is a tool capability (capabilityType = 15)
   223→	if bubble.CapabilityType == 15 {
   224→		toolText := processToolInvocation(bubble, capabilitiesMap, toolRegistry, composerVersion)
   225→		if toolText != "" {
   226→			parts = append(parts, toolText)
   227→		}
   228→	} else if bubble.Text != "" {
   229→		// Add main text if present (non-tool bubbles)
   230→		parts = append(parts, bubble.Text)
   231→	}
   232→
   233→	return strings.Join(parts, "\n\n---\n\n")
   234→}
   235→
   236→// processToolInvocation processes a tool invocation bubble and returns formatted markdown
   237→func processToolInvocation(bubble *ComposerConversation, capabilitiesMap map[int]*CapabilityData, toolRegistry *ToolRegistry, composerVersion int) string {
   238→	var toolData *BubbleConversation
   239→
   240→	// V3+ format: tool data is in bubble.ToolFormerData
   241→	if composerVersion >= 3 && bubble.ToolFormerData != nil {
   242→		toolData = convertToolInvocationData(bubble.ToolFormerData)
   243→	} else {
   244→		// V1 format: tool data is in capabilities[15].bubbleDataMap[bubbleId]
   245→		if capData, ok := capabilitiesMap[bubble.CapabilityType]; ok {
   246→			if capData.ParsedBubbleMap != nil {
   247→				if bubbleData, found := capData.ParsedBubbleMap[bubble.BubbleID]; found {
   248→					toolData = bubbleData
   249→				}
   250→			}
   251→		}
   252→	}
   253→
   254→	if toolData == nil {
   255→		slog.Warn("Tool invocation data not found",
   256→			"bubbleId", bubble.BubbleID,
   257→			"capabilityType", bubble.CapabilityType)
   258→		return bubble.Text // Fallback to original text
   259→	}
   260→
   261→	// Format the tool invocation using the registry
   262→	return FormatToolInvocation(toolData, toolRegistry)
   263→}
   264→
   265→// convertToolInvocationData converts ToolInvocationData to BubbleConversation
   266→func convertToolInvocationData(data *ToolInvocationData) *BubbleConversation {
   267→	return &BubbleConversation{
   268→		Tool:           data.Tool,
   269→		Name:           data.Name,
   270→		RawArgs:        data.RawArgs,
   271→		Params:         data.Params,
   272→		Result:         data.Result,
   273→		Status:         data.Status,
   274→		Error:          data.Error,
   275→		AdditionalData: data.AdditionalData,
   276→		UserDecision:   data.UserDecision,
   277→	}
   278→}
   279→
   280→// parseCapabilities parses the capabilities array and extracts tool data
   281→// Returns a map of capabilityType -> CapabilityData
   282→func parseCapabilities(composer *ComposerData) map[int]*CapabilityData {
   283→	capabilitiesMap := make(map[int]*CapabilityData)
   284→
   285→	for _, capability := range composer.Capabilities {
   286→		capData := capability.Data
   287→
   288→		// Parse bubbleDataMap if it's a string (JSON)
   289→		if capData.BubbleDataMap != nil {
   290→			if bubbleMapStr, ok := capData.BubbleDataMap.(string); ok {
   291→				// Parse the JSON string into a map
   292→				var bubbleMap map[string]*BubbleConversation
   293→				if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(bubbleMapStr), &bubbleMap); err != nil {
   294→					slog.Warn("Failed to parse bubbleDataMap",
   295→						"capabilityType", capability.Type,
   296→						"error", err)
   297→				} else {
   298→					capData.ParsedBubbleMap = bubbleMap
   299→				}
   300→			}
   301→		}
   302→
   303→		capabilitiesMap[capability.Type] = &capData
   304→	}
   305→
   306→	return capabilitiesMap
   307→}

   309→// calculateTimestamp calculates the absolute timestamp from timing info
   310→// Based on the TypeScript extension logic:
   311→// Sometimes clientStartTime is relative (< 946684800000 = Jan 1, 2000)
   312→// In that case, calculate absolute time as: clientEndTime - clientStartTime
   313→func calculateTimestamp(timingInfo *TimingInfo) string {
   314→	if timingInfo == nil {
   315→		return ""
   316→	}
   317→
   318→	clientStartTime := timingInfo.ClientStartTime
   319→	if clientStartTime == 0 {
   320→		return ""
   321→	}
   322→
   323→	// Check if clientStartTime is relative (< 946684800000, which is year 2000)
   324→	// e.g., full epoch: 1754311716540, relative: 1234.435
   325→	if clientStartTime < 946684800000 {
   326→		// Get clientEndTime (try fields in priority order)
   327→		var clientEndTime float64
   328→		if timingInfo.ClientRpcSendTime != 0 {
   329→			clientEndTime = timingInfo.ClientRpcSendTime
   330→		} else if timingInfo.ClientSettleTime != 0 {
   331→			clientEndTime = timingInfo.ClientSettleTime
   332→		} else if timingInfo.ClientEndTime != 0 {
   333→			clientEndTime = timingInfo.ClientEndTime
   334→		}
   335→
   336→		// Calculate absolute time
   337→		if clientEndTime != 0 {
   338→			clientStartTime = clientEndTime - clientStartTime
   339→		}
   340→	}
   341→
   342→	// Convert milliseconds to ISO 8601
   343→	// Split into seconds and fractional part for precise conversion
   344→	seconds := int64(clientStartTime / 1000)
   345→	nanos := int64((clientStartTime - float64(seconds)*1000) * 1000000)
   346→	t := time.Unix(seconds, nanos)
   347→	return t.Format(time.RFC3339)
   348→}
   349→
   350→// unifiedModeToString converts Cursor's unifiedMode number to a readable string
   351→// Based on the TypeScript extension logic (ts-extension/core/utils/composer.ts:118-132)
   352→// 1 = Ask, 2 = Agent, 5 = Plan, other = Custom
   353→func unifiedModeToString(unifiedMode int) string {
   354→	switch unifiedMode {
   355→	case 1:
   356→		return "Ask"
   357→	case 2:
   358→		return "Agent"
   359→	case 5:
   360→		return "Plan"
   361→	default:
   362→		if unifiedMode != 0 {
   363→			return "Custom"
   364→		}
   365→		return ""
   366→	}
   367→}

   107→// GetIntFromMap safely extracts an int from a map[string]interface{}.
   108→// JSON numbers are unmarshaled as float64, so we handle that case.
   109→func GetIntFromMap(m map[string]interface{}, key string) int {
   110→	if m == nil {
   111→		return 0
   112→	}
   113→	if val, ok := m[key]; ok {
   114→		switch v := val.(type) {
   115→		case float64:
   116→			return int(v)
   117→		case int64:
   118→			return int(v)
   119→		case int:
   120→			return v
   121→		}
   122→	}
   123→	return 0
   124→}

   147→// Validate checks the SessionData against schema constraints and logs warnings for any issues.
   148→// Returns true if validation passed, false if there were any issues.
   149→func (s *SessionData) Validate() bool {
   150→	valid := true
   151→
   152→	// Check schema version
   153→	if s.SchemaVersion != "1.0" {
   154→		slog.Warn("schema validation: schemaVersion must be '1.0'", "got", s.SchemaVersion)
   155→		valid = false
   156→	}
   157→
   158→	// Check required root fields
   159→	if s.Provider.ID == "" {
   160→		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.id is required")
   161→		valid = false
   162→	}
   163→	if s.Provider.Name == "" {
   164→		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.name is required")
   165→		valid = false
   166→	}
   167→	if s.Provider.Version == "" {
   168→		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.version is required")
   169→		valid = false
   170→	}
   171→	if s.SessionID == "" {
   172→		slog.Warn("schema validation: sessionId is required")
   173→		valid = false
   174→	}
   175→	if s.CreatedAt == "" {
   176→		slog.Warn("schema validation: createdAt is required")
   177→		valid = false
   178→	}
   179→	if s.WorkspaceRoot == "" {
   180→		slog.Warn("schema validation: workspaceRoot is required")
   181→		valid = false
   182→	}
   183→
   184→	// Validate each exchange
   185→	for i, exchange := range s.Exchanges {
   186→		if exchange.ExchangeID == "" {
   187→			slog.Warn("schema validation: exchange.exchangeId is required", "exchangeIndex", i)
   188→			valid = false
   189→		}
   190→
   191→		// Validate each message in the exchange
   192→		for j, msg := range exchange.Messages {
   193→			if !msg.validate(i, j) {
   194→				valid = false
   195→			}
   196→		}
   197→	}
   198→
   199→	return valid
   200→}
   201→
   202→// validate checks a single message against schema constraints.
   203→func (m *Message) validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex int) bool {
   204→	valid := true
   205→	logCtx := []any{"exchangeIndex", exchangeIndex, "messageIndex", messageIndex}
   206→
   207→	// Check role is valid
   208→	if m.Role != RoleUser && m.Role != RoleAgent {
   209→		slog.Warn("schema validation: message.role must be 'user' or 'agent'",
   210→			append(logCtx, "got", m.Role)...)
   211→		valid = false
   212→	}
   213→
   214→	// User message constraints
   215→	if m.Role == RoleUser {
   216→		if len(m.Content) == 0 {
   217→			slog.Warn("schema validation: user message must have non-empty content", logCtx...)
   218→			valid = false
   219→		}
   220→		if m.Tool != nil {
   221→			slog.Warn("schema validation: user message cannot have tool", logCtx...)
   222→			valid = false
   223→		}
   224→		if m.Model != "" {
   225→			slog.Warn("schema validation: user message cannot have model", logCtx...)
   226→			valid = false
   227→		}
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	// Agent message constraints: must have at least one of content, tool, or pathHints
   231→	if m.Role == RoleAgent {
   232→		hasContent := len(m.Content) > 0
   233→		hasTool := m.Tool != nil
   234→		hasPathHints := len(m.PathHints) > 0
   235→		if !hasContent && !hasTool && !hasPathHints {
   236→			slog.Warn("schema validation: agent message must have content, tool, or pathHints", logCtx...)
   237→			valid = false
   238→		}
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	// Validate content parts
   242→	for k, part := range m.Content {
   243→		if !part.validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex, k) {
   244→			valid = false
   245→		}
   246→	}
   247→
   248→	// Validate tool if present
   249→	if m.Tool != nil {
   250→		if !m.Tool.validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex) {
   251→			valid = false
   252→		}
   253→	}
   254→
   255→	return valid
   256→}
   257→
   258→// validate checks a single content part against schema constraints.
   259→func (c *ContentPart) validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex, partIndex int) bool {
   260→	valid := true
   261→	logCtx := []any{"exchangeIndex", exchangeIndex, "messageIndex", messageIndex, "partIndex", partIndex}
   262→
   263→	if c.Type != ContentTypeText && c.Type != ContentTypeThinking {
   264→		slog.Warn("schema validation: contentPart.type must be 'text' or 'thinking'",
   265→			append(logCtx, "got", c.Type)...)
   266→		valid = false
   267→	}
   268→
   269→	return valid
   270→}

   272→// validate checks tool info against schema constraints.

   203→		message.WriteString(formatEscapeJSONBlock(params))

   205→
   206→	// Add additional data section

   211→
   212→	// Parse and add result section

   224→	}

   229→	}

   239→		errorData := map[string]interface{}{"error": bubble.Error}
   240→		message.WriteString(formatEscapeJSONBlock(errorData))
   241→	}

   247→
   248→// formatEscapeJSONBlock formats JSON with escaped special characters
   249→// Matches the TypeScript formatEscapeJsonBlock function
   250→func formatEscapeJSONBlock(data map[string]interface{}) string {
   251→	// Marshal JSON with indentation
   252→	jsonBytes, err := json.MarshalIndent(data, "", "  ")
   253→	if err != nil {
   254→		return fmt.Sprintf("```json\n%v\n```\n", data)
   255→	}
   256→
   257→	// Escape special characters (backticks, <, >, &)
   258→	jsonStr := string(jsonBytes)
   259→	jsonStr = strings.ReplaceAll(jsonStr, "&", "&amp;")
   260→	jsonStr = strings.ReplaceAll(jsonStr, "`", "&#96;")
   261→	jsonStr = strings.ReplaceAll(jsonStr, "<", "&lt;")
   262→	jsonStr = strings.ReplaceAll(jsonStr, ">", "&gt;")
   263→
   264→	return fmt.Sprintf("```json\n%s\n```\n", jsonStr)
   265→}

The root cause is clear. In `agent_session.go`, tool bubbles (capabilityType == 15) only populate `message.Content` with formatted markdown text — `message.Tool` is **never set**. The telemetry stats functions (`extractToolInfo`, `countSessionTools`) exclusively check `msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.Name != ""`, so they always get zero.

Claude Code works because its provider properly sets `message.Tool` when processing tool use entries from the JSONL.

The fix is in `agent_session.go`:

1. Extract a `resolveToolData` helper (refactoring out the first half of `processToolInvocation`)
2. Add a `toSchemaToolType` converter (cursoride has "mcp" which isn't in the schema)
3. After building each message, if it's a tool bubble, also set `message.Tool`

Here's the approach:

Builds cleanly. The `interface{} can be replaced by any` diagnostic on line 138 is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this change — it's on the `Metadata` map in the `schema` package.

**Summary of the fix:**

The cursoride provider was rendering tool invocations as formatted markdown text in `message.Content`, but never setting `message.Tool`. Since `extractToolInfo` and `countSessionTools` only look at `msg.Tool`, all tool counts were 0.

The fix:
1. **Extracted `resolveToolData`** — pulls the `BubbleConversation` (tool name, params, etc.) from either V3+ `ToolFormerData` or V1 capabilities map. `processToolInvocation` now calls this instead of duplicating the logic.
2. **Added `toSchemaToolType`** — maps cursoride's `ToolType` to schema constants; the only difference is `"mcp"` → `"generic"` since the schema has no mcp type.
3. **Set `message.Tool`** — after building each message, if it's a tool bubble (capabilityType 15), resolves the tool data and sets `message.Tool = &schema.ToolInfo{Name: ..., Type: ...}`. The formatted markdown stays in `Content` as before; `Tool` carries the structured metadata for telemetry.

    25→// MessageTimestampCache tracks first-seen wall clock times for Cursor messages.
    26→// Cursor's SQLite data doesn't include per-message timestamps, so in run/watch
    27→// mode we stamp each message with time.Now() when we first see it. The cache
    28→// ensures that when the session is regenerated (the entire session is rebuilt
    29→// on each poll), previously-seen messages retain their original timestamp.
    30→type MessageTimestampCache struct {
    31→	mu    sync.Mutex
    32→	times map[string]time.Time
    33→}
    34→
    35→func NewMessageTimestampCache() *MessageTimestampCache {
    36→	return &MessageTimestampCache{times: make(map[string]time.Time)}
    37→}
    38→
    39→// Stamp returns the first-seen timestamp for a message ID.
    40→// First call for a given ID records time.Now(); subsequent calls return the cached value.
    41→func (c *MessageTimestampCache) Stamp(messageID string) time.Time {
    42→	c.mu.Lock()
    43→	defer c.mu.Unlock()
    44→	if t, ok := c.times[messageID]; ok {
    45→		return t
    46→	}
    47→	now := time.Now()
    48→	c.times[messageID] = now
    49→	return now
    50→}

   111→// assignTimestamps fills in Message.Timestamp and Exchange start/end times for
   112→// run/watch mode only. Cursor's data doesn't include per-message timestamps,
   113→// so we use wall clock time when each message is first seen. The cache ensures
   114→// previously-seen messages retain their original timestamp across session
   115→// regenerations. When tsCache is nil (sync mode), timestamps are left empty
   116→// so they don't render in the markdown output.
   117→func assignTimestamps(sd *SessionData, tsCache *MessageTimestampCache) {
   118→	if tsCache == nil {
   119→		return
   120→	}
   121→	for i := range sd.Exchanges {
   122→		ex := &sd.Exchanges[i]
   123→		for j := range ex.Messages {
   124→			msg := &ex.Messages[j]
   125→			if msg.Timestamp == "" {
   126→				msg.Timestamp = tsCache.Stamp(msg.ID).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
   127→			}
   128→		}
   129→		if len(ex.Messages) > 0 {
   130→			if ex.StartTime == "" {
   131→				ex.StartTime = ex.Messages[0].Timestamp
   132→			}
   133→			if ex.EndTime == "" {
   134→				ex.EndTime = ex.Messages[len(ex.Messages)-1].Timestamp
   135→			}
   136→		}
   137→	}
   138→}

   140→// buildExchangesFromBlobs groups blob records into exchanges
   141→// An exchange is a user prompt followed by agent responses and tool results
   142→// Blob records are already in DAG-sorted order from ReadSessionData
   143→func buildExchangesFromBlobs(blobRecords []BlobRecord, workspaceRoot string) ([]Exchange, error) {
   144→	var exchanges []Exchange
   145→	var currentExchange *Exchange
   146→
   147→	// Track pending tool calls that need results merged
   148→	type pendingTool struct {
   149→		exchangeIdx int
   150→		messageIdx  int
   151→		toolCallID  string
   152→	}
   153→	pendingTools := make(map[string]pendingTool)
   154→
   155→	for _, record := range blobRecords {

   158→			Role    string            `json:"role"`
   159→			ID      string            `json:"id"`
   160→			Content []json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
   161→		}
   162→
   163→		if err := json.Unmarshal(record.Data, &data); err != nil {
   164→			slog.Debug("Failed to parse blob record", "rowid", record.RowID, "error", err)
   165→			continue
   166→		}
   167→
   168→		// Skip if no content
   169→		if len(data.Content) == 0 {
   170→			continue
   171→		}
   172→
   173→		switch data.Role {
   174→		case "user":
   175→			// Check if this is a real user message or just metadata
   176→			firstContent, skipMsg := parseFirstContent(data.Content[0])
   177→			if skipMsg || (firstContent.Type == "text" && strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(firstContent.Text), "<user_info>")) {
   178→				continue
   179→			}
   180→
   181→			// This is a new user prompt, start a new exchange
   182→			if currentExchange != nil && len(currentExchange.Messages) > 0 {
   183→				exchanges = append(exchanges, *currentExchange)
   184→			}
   185→
   186→			currentExchange = &Exchange{
   187→				Messages: []Message{},
   188→			}
   189→
   190→			msg := buildUserMessageFromBlob(data.Content, record.RowID)
   191→			currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, msg)
   192→			if msg.Timestamp != "" {
   193→				currentExchange.StartTime = msg.Timestamp
   194→			}
   195→
   196→		case "assistant":
   197→			// Agent message - add to current exchange
   198→			if currentExchange == nil {
   199→				// Create exchange if we don't have one (shouldn't happen normally)
   200→				currentExchange = &Exchange{
   201→					Messages: []Message{},
   202→				}
   203→			}
   204→
   205→			// Build messages from this assistant blob (may return multiple if there are multiple tool calls)
   206→			msgs := buildAgentMessagesFromBlob(data.Content, record.RowID, workspaceRoot)
   207→
   208→			// Add all messages and track tool calls
   209→			for _, msg := range msgs {
   210→				// Track tool calls for later result merging
   211→				if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID != "" {
   212→					pendingTools[msg.Tool.UseID] = pendingTool{
   213→						exchangeIdx: len(exchanges),
   214→						messageIdx:  len(currentExchange.Messages),
   215→						toolCallID:  msg.Tool.UseID,
   216→					}
   217→				}
   218→
   219→				currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, msg)
   220→				if msg.Timestamp != "" {
   221→					currentExchange.EndTime = msg.Timestamp
   222→				}
   223→			}
   224→
   225→		case "tool":
   226→			// Tool result - merge into the corresponding tool use
   227→			if currentExchange == nil {
   228→				continue
   229→			}
   230→
   231→			// Extract tool result content
   232→			for _, contentRaw := range data.Content {
   233→				var contentItem struct {
   234→					Type       string `json:"type"`
   235→					ToolCallID string `json:"toolCallId"`
   236→					ToolName   string `json:"toolName"`
   237→					Result     string `json:"result"`
   238→				}
   239→
   240→				if err := json.Unmarshal(contentRaw, &contentItem); err != nil {
   241→					continue
   242→				}
   243→
   244→				if contentItem.Type == "tool-result" && contentItem.ToolCallID != "" {

   246→					if pending, ok := pendingTools[contentItem.ToolCallID]; ok {
   247→						// Merge result into the tool message
   248→						mergeToolResultIntoMessage(currentExchange, pending.messageIdx, contentItem.Result, contentItem.ToolName)

   250→					}
   251→				}
   252→			}
   253→		}
   254→	}
   255→
   256→	// Add the last exchange if it exists
   257→	if currentExchange != nil && len(currentExchange.Messages) > 0 {
   258→		exchanges = append(exchanges, *currentExchange)
   259→	}
   260→
   261→	// Blob records are already in DAG-sorted order, so exchanges are too
   262→	return exchanges, nil
   263→}
   264→
   265→// parseFirstContent parses the first content item to check if message should be skipped
   266→func parseFirstContent(contentRaw json.RawMessage) (ContentPart, bool) {
   267→	var contentItem struct {
   268→		Type string `json:"type"`
   269→		Text string `json:"text"`
   270→	}
   271→
   272→	if err := json.Unmarshal(contentRaw, &contentItem); err != nil {
   273→		return ContentPart{}, false
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Skip if it's user_info
   277→	if contentItem.Type == "text" && strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(contentItem.Text), "<user_info>") {
   278→		return ContentPart{Type: "text", Text: contentItem.Text}, true
   279→	}
   280→
   281→	return ContentPart{Type: contentItem.Type, Text: contentItem.Text}, false
   282→}
   283→
   284→// buildUserMessageFromBlob creates a Message from a user blob
   285→func buildUserMessageFromBlob(content []json.RawMessage, rowID int) Message {
   286→	var contentParts []ContentPart
   287→
   288→	for _, contentRaw := range content {
   289→		var contentItem struct {
   290→			Type string `json:"type"`
   291→			Text string `json:"text"`
   292→		}
   293→
   294→		if err := json.Unmarshal(contentRaw, &contentItem); err != nil {
   295→			continue
   296→		}
   297→
   298→		if contentItem.Type == "text" && contentItem.Text != "" {
   299→			// Strip user_query tags if present
   300→			cleanedText := stripUserQueryTags(contentItem.Text)
   301→			if cleanedText != "" {
   302→				contentParts = append(contentParts, ContentPart{
   303→					Type: "text",
   304→					Text: cleanedText,
   305→				})
   306→			}
   307→		}
   308→	}
   309→
   310→	return Message{
   311→		ID:      fmt.Sprintf("row-%d", rowID),
   312→		Role:    "user",
   313→		Content: contentParts,
   314→	}
   315→}
   316→
   317→// buildAgentMessagesFromBlob creates Messages from an assistant blob
   318→// When there are multiple tool-calls in a single assistant message, this creates
   319→// one text message followed by separate messages for each tool call
   320→func buildAgentMessagesFromBlob(content []json.RawMessage, rowID int, workspaceRoot string) []Message {
   321→	var messages []Message
   322→	var contentParts []ContentPart
   323→	toolCallIndex := 0
   324→
   325→	for _, contentRaw := range content {
   326→		var contentItem struct {
   327→			Type       string          `json:"type"`
   328→			Text       string          `json:"text"`
   329→			ToolName   string          `json:"toolName"`
   330→			ToolCallID string          `json:"toolCallId"`
   331→			Args       json.RawMessage `json:"args"`
   332→		}
   333→
   334→		if err := json.Unmarshal(contentRaw, &contentItem); err != nil {
   335→			continue
   336→		}
   337→
   338→		switch contentItem.Type {
   339→		case "text":
   340→			if contentItem.Text != "" {
   341→				contentParts = append(contentParts, ContentPart{
   342→					Type: "text",
   343→					Text: contentItem.Text,
   344→				})
   345→			}
   346→
   347→		case "reasoning":
   348→			// Preserve reasoning content as thinking type (schema canonical name)
   349→			if contentItem.Text != "" {
   350→				contentParts = append(contentParts, ContentPart{
   351→					Type: "thinking",
   352→					Text: contentItem.Text,
   353→				})
   354→			}
   355→
   356→		case "tool-call":
   357→			// Parse tool arguments
   358→			var toolInput map[string]interface{}
   359→			if err := json.Unmarshal(contentItem.Args, &toolInput); err != nil {
   360→				continue
   361→			}
   362→
   363→			// Create a separate message for this tool call
   364→			toolMsg := Message{
   365→				ID:   fmt.Sprintf("row-%d-tool-%d", rowID, toolCallIndex),
   366→				Role: "agent",
   367→				Tool: &ToolInfo{
   368→					Name:  contentItem.ToolName,
   369→					Type:  classifyCursorToolType(contentItem.ToolName),
   370→					UseID: contentItem.ToolCallID,
   371→					Input: toolInput,
   372→				},
   373→				PathHints: extractCursorPathHints(toolInput, workspaceRoot),
   374→			}
   375→
   376→			messages = append(messages, toolMsg)
   377→			toolCallIndex++
   378→		}
   379→	}
   380→
   381→	// If there's text content, create a text message first
   382→	if len(contentParts) > 0 {
   383→		textMsg := Message{
   384→			ID:      fmt.Sprintf("row-%d", rowID),
   385→			Role:    "agent",
   386→			Content: contentParts,
   387→		}
   388→		// Insert text message at the beginning
   389→		messages = append([]Message{textMsg}, messages...)
   390→	}
   391→
   392→	// If no messages were created (shouldn't happen), return an empty text message
   393→	if len(messages) == 0 {
   394→		messages = append(messages, Message{
   395→			ID:      fmt.Sprintf("row-%d", rowID),
   396→			Role:    "agent",
   397→			Content: []ContentPart{},
   398→		})
   399→	}
   400→
   401→	return messages
   402→}
   403→
   404→// mergeToolResultIntoMessage merges a tool result into a tool use message
   405→func mergeToolResultIntoMessage(exchange *Exchange, messageIdx int, result, toolName string) {
   406→	if messageIdx >= len(exchange.Messages) {
   407→		return
   408→	}
   409→
   410→	msg := &exchange.Messages[messageIdx]
   411→	if msg.Tool == nil {
   412→		return
   413→	}
   414→
   415→	// Skip TodoWrite errors
   416→	if toolName == "TodoWrite" && strings.HasPrefix(result, "Invalid arguments:") {
   417→		return
   418→	}
   419→
   420→	// Clean TodoWrite results
   421→	if toolName == "TodoWrite" {
   422→		result = cleanTodoResult(result)
   423→	}
   424→
   425→	// Add the output to the tool
   426→	msg.Tool.Output = map[string]interface{}{
   427→		"content": result,
   428→	}
   429→}
   430→
   431→// classifyCursorToolType maps Cursor tool names to standard tool types
   432→func classifyCursorToolType(toolName string) string {
   433→	switch toolName {
   434→	case "Write", "StrReplace", "MultiStrReplace":
   435→		return "write"
   436→	case "Read":
   437→		return "read"
   438→	case "Grep", "Glob":
   439→		return "search"
   440→	case "Shell", "LS":
   441→		return "shell"
   442→	case "Delete":
   443→		return "write" // Delete is a write operation
   444→	case "TodoWrite":
   445→		return "task"
   446→	default:
   447→		return "unknown"
   448→	}
   449→}
   450→
   451→// extractCursorPathHints extracts file paths from Cursor tool input
   452→func extractCursorPathHints(input map[string]interface{}, workspaceRoot string) []string {
   453→	var paths []string
   454→
   455→	// Common path field names in Cursor tools
   456→	pathFields := []string{"path", "file_path"}
   457→
   458→	for _, field := range pathFields {
   459→		if value, ok := input[field].(string); ok && value != "" {
   460→			normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(value, workspaceRoot)
   461→			if !containsPath(paths, normalizedPath) {
   462→				paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
   463→			}
   464→		}
   465→	}
   466→
   467→	// Handle MultiStrReplace paths array
   468→	if pathsArray, ok := input["paths"].([]interface{}); ok {
   469→		for _, item := range pathsArray {
   470→			if pathObj, ok := item.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
   471→				if filePath, ok := pathObj["file_path"].(string); ok && filePath != "" {
   472→					normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(filePath, workspaceRoot)
   473→					if !containsPath(paths, normalizedPath) {
   474→						paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
   475→					}
   476→				}
   477→			}
   478→		}
   479→	}
   480→
   481→	// Extract paths from shell commands (redirect targets, file-creating commands).
   482→	// Cursor's Shell tool input only contains "command" and "description" — no CWD field.
   483→	// The tool result also lacks CWD info. So we fall back to workspaceRoot as the best
   484→	// approximation. This means relative paths in commands run after a `cd` will resolve
   485→	// against the wrong directory, but there's nothing better available from Cursor's data.
   486→	if command, ok := input["command"].(string); ok && command != "" {
   487→		shellPaths := spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, workspaceRoot, workspaceRoot)
   488→		for _, sp := range shellPaths {
   489→			if !containsPath(paths, sp) {
   490→				paths = append(paths, sp)
   491→			}
   492→		}
   493→	}
   494→
   495→	return paths
   496→}
   497→
   498→// containsPath checks if a string slice contains a path
   499→func containsPath(slice []string, value string) bool {
   500→	for _, item := range slice {
   501→		if item == value {
   502→			return true
   503→		}
   504→	}
   505→	return false
   506→}
   507→
   508→// formatCursorToolWithSummary generates custom summary and formatted markdown for a Cursor tool
   509→// Returns (summary, formattedMarkdown) where summary is the custom content for <summary> tag
   510→// and formattedMarkdown is additional content to display in the tool-use block
   511→func formatCursorToolWithSummary(tool *ToolInfo) (string, string) {
   512→	var summary string
   513→	var formattedMd strings.Builder
   514→
   515→	// Format tool use based on tool name using existing Cursor formatters
   516→	// These formatters return custom summary content (without "Tool use: **Name**" prefix)
   517→	if tool.Input != nil {
   518→		switch tool.Name {
   519→		case "Write":
   520→			// Write tool: summary has file path, formatted content has code block
   521→			if path, ok := tool.Input["path"].(string); ok && path != "" {
   522→				summary = fmt.Sprintf("`%s`", path)
   523→			}
   524→			formattedMd.WriteString(formatWriteTool(tool.Input))
   525→		case "StrReplace":
   526→			// StrReplace tool: summary is empty, formatted content has diff
   527→			formattedMd.WriteString(formatStrReplaceTool(tool.Input))
   528→		case "Delete":
   529→			// Delete tool: summary has path, no formatted content
   530→			summary = formatDeleteTool(tool.Input)
   531→		case "Grep":
   532→			// Grep tool: summary has search details, no formatted content
   533→			summary = formatGrepTool(tool.Input)
   534→		case "Glob":
   535→			// Glob tool: summary has pattern, no formatted content
   536→			summary = formatGlobTool(tool.Input)
   537→		case "Read":
   538→			// Read tool: summary has file path, no formatted content
   539→			summary = formatReadTool(tool.Input)
   540→		case "LS":
   541→			// LS tool: summary has directory, no formatted content
   542→			summary = formatLSTool(tool.Input)
   543→		case "Shell":
   544→			// Shell tool: summary has command, no formatted content
   545→			summary = formatShellTool(tool.Input)
   546→		case "MultiStrReplace":
   547→			// MultiStrReplace tool: summary has file and edits, no formatted content
   548→			summary = formatMultiStrReplaceTool(tool.Input)
   549→		case "TodoWrite":
   550→			// Handle TodoWrite specially
   551→			if todos, ok := tool.Input["todos"].([]interface{}); ok && len(todos) > 0 {
   552→				formattedMd.WriteString(formatTodoList(todos))
   553→			}
   554→		}
   555→	}
   556→
   557→	// Add tool result/output if present
   558→	if tool.Output != nil {
   559→		if content, ok := tool.Output["content"].(string); ok && content != "" {
   560→			if formattedMd.Len() > 0 {
   561→				formattedMd.WriteString("\n\n")
   562→			}
   563→			// Format based on tool type
   564→			switch tool.Name {
   565→			case "TodoWrite":
   566→				// TodoWrite results are already formatted
   567→				formattedMd.WriteString(content)
   568→			case "Grep":
   569→				// Grep results have special formatting
   570→				formattedMd.WriteString(formatGrepResult(content))
   571→			case "Glob":
   572→				// Glob results are inline
   573→				formattedMd.WriteString(strings.TrimSpace(content))
   574→			case "Delete":
   575→				// Delete results are inline
   576→				formattedMd.WriteString(content)
   577→			default:
   578→				// Default: wrap in code block
   579→				formattedMd.WriteString(formatToolResult(content))
   580→			}
   581→		}
   582→	}
   583→
   584→	// If we have a custom summary, prepend "Tool use: **ToolName**" prefix
   585→	if summary != "" {
   586→		summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** %s", tool.Name, summary)
   587→	}
   588→
   589→	return summary, strings.TrimSpace(formattedMd.String())
   590→}
   591→
   592→// stripUserQueryTags removes <user_query> tags from text content
   593→// These tags are added by Cursor CLI to wrap user input, but we don't want them in the markdown output
   594→func stripUserQueryTags(text string) string {
   595→	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(text)
   596→
   597→	// Check if text is wrapped with user_query tags
   598→	if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<user_query>") && strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "</user_query>") {
   599→		// Remove opening tag and any trailing newline
   600→		content := strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "<user_query>")
   601→		content = strings.TrimPrefix(content, "\n")
   602→
   603→		// Remove closing tag and any preceding newline
   604→		content = strings.TrimSuffix(content, "</user_query>")
   605→		content = strings.TrimSuffix(content, "\n")
   606→
   607→		return content
   608→	}
   609→
   610→	// Return original text if tags aren't present
   611→	return text
   612→}

   129→	slog.Info("GenerateAgentSession: Built exchanges", "count", len(exchanges))
   130→
   131→	sessionData := &SessionData{
   132→		SchemaVersion: "1.0",
   133→		Provider: ProviderInfo{
   134→			ID:      "codex-cli",
   135→			Name:    "Codex CLI",
   136→			Version: "unknown", // Codex doesn't currently include version in JSONL
   137→		},
   138→		SessionID:     sessionID,
   139→		CreatedAt:     createdAt,
   140→		WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
   141→		Exchanges:     exchanges,
   142→	}
   143→
   144→	return sessionData, nil
   145→}

   147→// extractSessionMetadata parses the session_meta record (first line)
   148→func extractSessionMetadata(records []map[string]interface{}) (sessionID, createdAt, cwd string, err error) {
   149→	if len(records) == 0 {
   150→		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("no records to extract metadata from")
   151→	}
   152→
   153→	firstRecord := records[0]
   154→	recordType, ok := firstRecord["type"].(string)
   155→	if !ok || recordType != "session_meta" {
   156→		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("first record is not session_meta: %v", recordType)
   157→	}
   158→
   159→	payload, ok := firstRecord["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
   160→	if !ok {
   161→		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("session_meta payload is missing or invalid")
   162→	}
   163→
   164→	sessionID, _ = payload["id"].(string)
   165→	createdAt, _ = payload["timestamp"].(string)
   166→	cwd, _ = payload["cwd"].(string)
   167→
   168→	if sessionID == "" {
   169→		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("session_meta is missing session ID")
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	if createdAt == "" {
   173→		// Fall back to record timestamp
   174→		createdAt, _ = firstRecord["timestamp"].(string)
   175→	}
   176→
   177→	return sessionID, createdAt, cwd, nil
   178→}
   179→
   180→// buildExchangesFromRecords groups JSONL records into exchanges
   181→// An exchange starts with a user message and contains all subsequent agent responses and tool uses
   182→func buildExchangesFromRecords(records []map[string]interface{}, workspaceRoot string) ([]Exchange, error) {
   183→	var exchanges []Exchange
   184→	var currentExchange *Exchange
   185→	var currentModel string
   186→	pendingTools := make(map[string]*PendingToolCall) // callID -> pending tool call
   187→
   188→	for i, record := range records {
   189→		recordType, _ := record["type"].(string)
   190→		timestamp, _ := record["timestamp"].(string)
   191→
   192→		switch recordType {
   193→		case "session_meta":
   194→			// Skip session metadata - already processed
   195→			continue
   196→
   197→		case "turn_context":
   198→			// Update current model for subsequent agent messages
   199→			payload, ok := record["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
   200→			if ok {
   201→				if model, ok := payload["model"].(string); ok {
   202→					currentModel = model
   203→					slog.Debug("Updated current model", "model", currentModel)
   204→				}
   205→			}
   206→			continue
   207→
   208→		case "event_msg":
   209→			// Handle user messages, agent messages, and agent reasoning
   210→			payload, ok := record["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
   211→			if !ok {
   212→				continue
   213→			}
   214→
   215→			payloadType, _ := payload["type"].(string)
   216→
   217→			switch payloadType {
   218→			case "user_message":
   219→				// Start a new exchange
   220→				message, ok := payload["message"].(string)
   221→				if !ok || message == "" {
   222→					continue
   223→				}
   224→
   225→				// Save previous exchange if exists
   226→				if currentExchange != nil && len(currentExchange.Messages) > 0 {
   227→					exchanges = append(exchanges, *currentExchange)
   228→				}
   229→
   230→				// Start new exchange
   231→				currentExchange = &Exchange{
   232→					StartTime: timestamp,
   233→					Messages:  []Message{},
   234→				}
   235→
   236→				// Add user message
   237→				userMsg := Message{
   238→					ID:        fmt.Sprintf("u_%d", i),
   239→					Timestamp: timestamp,
   240→					Role:      "user",
   241→					Content: []ContentPart{
   242→						{Type: "text", Text: message},
   243→					},
   244→				}
   245→				currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, userMsg)
   246→
   247→			case "agent_message":
   248→				// Agent text response - keep as separate message per user's requirement
   249→				message, ok := payload["message"].(string)
   250→				if !ok || message == "" {
   251→					continue
   252→				}
   253→
   254→				if currentExchange == nil {
   255→					// Create exchange if missing (shouldn't happen)
   256→					currentExchange = &Exchange{
   257→						StartTime: timestamp,
   258→						Messages:  []Message{},
   259→					}
   260→				}
   261→
   262→				agentMsg := Message{
   263→					ID:        fmt.Sprintf("a_%d", i),
   264→					Timestamp: timestamp,
   265→					Role:      "agent",
   266→					Model:     currentModel,
   267→					Content: []ContentPart{
   268→						{Type: "text", Text: message},
   269→					},
   270→				}
   271→				currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, agentMsg)
   272→				currentExchange.EndTime = timestamp
   273→
   274→			case "agent_reasoning":
   275→				// Agent thinking - keep as separate message with thinking content type
   276→				text, ok := payload["text"].(string)
   277→				if !ok || text == "" {
   278→					continue
   279→				}
   280→
   281→				if currentExchange == nil {
   282→					// Create exchange if missing (shouldn't happen)
   283→					currentExchange = &Exchange{
   284→						StartTime: timestamp,
   285→						Messages:  []Message{},
   286→					}
   287→				}
   288→
   289→				reasoningMsg := Message{
   290→					ID:        fmt.Sprintf("r_%d", i),
   291→					Timestamp: timestamp,
   292→					Role:      "agent",
   293→					Model:     currentModel,
   294→					Content: []ContentPart{
   295→						{Type: "thinking", Text: text},
   296→					},
   297→				}
   298→				currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, reasoningMsg)
   299→				currentExchange.EndTime = timestamp
   300→
   301→			case "token_count":
   302→				// Token usage event - attach to the most recent agent message
   303→				if currentExchange == nil || len(currentExchange.Messages) == 0 {
   304→					continue
   305→				}
   306→
   307→				usage := extractUsageFromTokenCount(payload)
   308→				if usage == nil {
   309→					continue
   310→				}
   311→
   312→				// Find the most recent agent message to attach usage to
   313→				for j := len(currentExchange.Messages) - 1; j >= 0; j-- {
   314→					if currentExchange.Messages[j].Role == "agent" {
   315→						currentExchange.Messages[j].Usage = usage
   316→						slog.Debug("Attached token usage to agent message",
   317→							"messageID", currentExchange.Messages[j].ID,
   318→							"inputTokens", usage.InputTokens,
   319→							"outputTokens", usage.OutputTokens,
   320→							"cachedInputTokens", usage.CachedInputTokens,
   321→							"reasoningOutputTokens", usage.ReasoningOutputTokens)
   322→						break
   323→					}
   324→				}
   325→			}
   326→
   327→		case "response_item":
   328→			// Handle function calls and custom tool calls
   329→			payload, ok := record["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
   330→			if !ok {
   331→				continue
   332→			}
   333→
   334→			payloadType, _ := payload["type"].(string)
   335→
   336→			switch payloadType {
   337→			case "function_call":
   338→				// Function call (e.g., shell command)
   339→				if currentExchange == nil {
   340→					currentExchange = &Exchange{
   341→						StartTime: timestamp,
   342→						Messages:  []Message{},
   343→					}
   344→				}
   345→
   346→				toolName, _ := payload["name"].(string)
   347→				argumentsJSON, _ := payload["arguments"].(string)
   348→				callID, _ := payload["call_id"].(string)
   349→
   350→				if toolName == "" {
   351→					continue
   352→				}
   353→
   354→				// Parse arguments to extract input
   355→				var input map[string]interface{}
   356→				if argumentsJSON != "" {
   357→					if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(argumentsJSON), &input); err != nil {
   358→						slog.Warn("Failed to parse function call arguments", "error", err, "arguments", argumentsJSON)
   359→						input = map[string]interface{}{"raw": argumentsJSON}
   360→					}
   361→				}
   362→
   363→				// Create tool message
   364→				toolMsg := Message{
   365→					ID:        fmt.Sprintf("t_%d", i),
   366→					Timestamp: timestamp,
   367→					Role:      "agent",
   368→					Model:     currentModel,
   369→					Tool: &ToolInfo{
   370→						Name:   toolName,
   371→						Type:   classifyToolType(toolName),
   372→						UseID:  callID,
   373→						Input:  input,
   374→						Output: nil, // Will be filled when we find the output
   375→					},
   376→					PathHints: extractPathHints(toolName, input, "", workspaceRoot),
   377→				}
   378→
   379→				currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, toolMsg)
   380→				currentExchange.EndTime = timestamp
   381→
   382→				// Track this tool call to match with output later
   383→				if callID != "" {
   384→					pendingTools[callID] = &PendingToolCall{
   385→						message:   &currentExchange.Messages[len(currentExchange.Messages)-1],
   386→						toolInfo:  currentExchange.Messages[len(currentExchange.Messages)-1].Tool,
   387→						timestamp: timestamp,
   388→					}
   389→				}
   390→
   391→			case "function_call_output":
   392→				// Function call output - merge into the pending tool call
   393→				callID, _ := payload["call_id"].(string)
   394→				outputJSON, _ := payload["output"].(string)
   395→
   396→				if callID == "" || outputJSON == "" {
   397→					continue
   398→				}
   399→
   400→				// Find the pending tool call
   401→				if pending, exists := pendingTools[callID]; exists {
   402→					// Parse the output JSON
   403→					var outputData map[string]interface{}
   404→					if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(outputJSON), &outputData); err == nil {
   405→						pending.toolInfo.Output = outputData
   406→					} else {
   407→						pending.toolInfo.Output = map[string]interface{}{"raw": outputJSON}
   408→					}
   409→					delete(pendingTools, callID)
   410→				}
   411→
   412→			case "custom_tool_call":
   413→				// Custom tool call (e.g., apply_patch)
   414→				if currentExchange == nil {
   415→					currentExchange = &Exchange{
   416→						StartTime: timestamp,
   417→						Messages:  []Message{},
   418→					}
   419→				}
   420→
   421→				toolName, _ := payload["name"].(string)
   422→				inputText, _ := payload["input"].(string)
   423→				callID, _ := payload["call_id"].(string)
   424→
   425→				if toolName == "" {
   426→					continue
   427→				}
   428→
   429→				// For custom tools, input is plain text, not JSON
   430→				input := map[string]interface{}{
   431→					"input": inputText,
   432→				}
   433→
   434→				// Create tool message
   435→				toolMsg := Message{
   436→					ID:        fmt.Sprintf("ct_%d", i),
   437→					Timestamp: timestamp,
   438→					Role:      "agent",
   439→					Model:     currentModel,
   440→					Tool: &ToolInfo{
   441→						Name:   toolName,
   442→						Type:   classifyToolType(toolName),
   443→						UseID:  callID,
   444→						Input:  input,
   445→						Output: nil, // Will be filled when we find the output
   446→					},
   447→					PathHints: extractPathHints(toolName, input, inputText, workspaceRoot),
   448→				}
   449→
   450→				currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, toolMsg)
   451→				currentExchange.EndTime = timestamp
   452→
   453→				// Track this tool call to match with output later
   454→				if callID != "" {
   455→					pendingTools[callID] = &PendingToolCall{
   456→						message:   &currentExchange.Messages[len(currentExchange.Messages)-1],
   457→						toolInfo:  currentExchange.Messages[len(currentExchange.Messages)-1].Tool,
   458→						timestamp: timestamp,
   459→					}
   460→				}
   461→
   462→			case "custom_tool_call_output":
   463→				// Custom tool call output - merge into the pending tool call
   464→				callID, _ := payload["call_id"].(string)
   465→				outputJSON, _ := payload["output"].(string)
   466→
   467→				if callID == "" || outputJSON == "" {
   468→					continue
   469→				}
   470→
   471→				// Find the pending tool call
   472→				if pending, exists := pendingTools[callID]; exists {
   473→					// Parse the output JSON
   474→					var outputData map[string]interface{}
   475→					if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(outputJSON), &outputData); err == nil {
   476→						pending.toolInfo.Output = outputData
   477→					} else {
   478→						pending.toolInfo.Output = map[string]interface{}{"raw": outputJSON}
   479→					}
   480→					delete(pendingTools, callID)
   481→				}
   482→			}
   483→		}
   484→	}
   485→
   486→	// Add the last exchange if exists
   487→	if currentExchange != nil && len(currentExchange.Messages) > 0 {
   488→		exchanges = append(exchanges, *currentExchange)
   489→	}
   490→
   491→	return exchanges, nil
   492→}

   494→// formatToolWithSummary generates custom summary and formatted markdown for a Codex tool
   495→// Returns (summary, formattedMarkdown) where summary is the custom content for <summary> tag
   496→// and formattedMarkdown is additional content to display in the tool-use block
   497→func formatToolWithSummary(tool *ToolInfo, workspaceRoot string) (string, string) {
   498→	var summary string
   499→	var formattedMd strings.Builder
   500→
   501→	// Format tool input based on whether it's a function call or custom tool
   502→	if tool.Input != nil {
   503→		// Check if this is a custom tool (has string input in "input" field)
   504→		if inputStr, ok := tool.Input["input"].(string); ok {
   505→			// Custom tool with text input (e.g., apply_patch)
   506→			formattedMd.WriteString(formatCustomToolCall(tool.Name, inputStr))
   507→		} else if tool.Name == "shell_command" || tool.Name == "exec_command" {
   508→			// Shell command: normalize "cmd" → "command" for exec_command
   509→			toolInput := tool.Input
   510→			if _, ok := toolInput["cmd"]; ok {
   511→				if _, hasCommand := toolInput["command"]; !hasCommand {
   512→					toolInput["command"] = toolInput["cmd"]
   513→				}
   514→			}
   515→			inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(toolInput)
   516→			shellSummary, shellBody := formatShellWithSummary(string(inputJSON))
   517→			if shellSummary != "" {
   518→				// Single-line command goes in summary
   519→				summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** %s", tool.Name, shellSummary)
   520→			}
   521→			if shellBody != "" {
   522→				formattedMd.WriteString(shellBody)
   523→			}
   524→		} else {
   525→			// Other function calls with JSON arguments
   526→			inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(tool.Input)
   527→			formattedMd.WriteString(formatToolCall(tool.Name, string(inputJSON)))
   528→		}
   529→	}
   530→
   531→	// Format tool output if present
   532→	if tool.Output != nil {
   533→		if outputStr, ok := tool.Output["raw"].(string); ok {
   534→			// Clean and truncate output if needed
   535→			cleaned := strings.TrimSpace(outputStr)
   536→			// Only show output if there's actual content
   537→			if cleaned != "" {
   538→				if formattedMd.Len() > 0 {
   539→					formattedMd.WriteString("\n")
   540→				}
   541→				if len(cleaned) > 5000 {
   542→					cleaned = cleaned[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
   543→				}
   544→				formattedMd.WriteString("```\n" + cleaned + "\n```")
   545→			}
   546→		}
   547→	}
   548→
   549→	return summary, strings.TrimSpace(formattedMd.String())
   550→}
